_README: PLACEHOLDER LINES for the player character's voice-over (the character talks to themselves while exploring). Every line here can be rewritten by Marius, Chris or Martin: change the text, save, then run  build/make_vo.py  to regenerate the computer-voice audio and the word timings (only changed lines are redone). FIELDS: id = unique name (also the audio file name: voice/vo/<id>.m4a); who = 'chris' | 'martin' | 'both' (Marius plays with Chris's lines; 'both' lines are generated once per person as <id>_chris / <id>_martin); trigger = when it can play; day = [first day, last day] it may play, using the December date (0 = any time, so lines that must not spoil anything are gated); text = the words; mood = a note for whoever records it (not used by the game). Each line plays once per player (saved as kv-vo-seen). TRIGGERS: place:<tree|bowling|church|bridge|botnan|orre|globen|penstock|hamre|feda|home_chris_up|home_chris_down|home_martin|market|cairn> (first arrival; home_chris_up = Chris's flat, home_chris_down = the ground floor with the witch); event:<hollow_seen|scream_freeze|lamp_safe|flare|notebook|thermos|snowball|rocket|threshold_on|threshold_off|witch_scream|witch_defeated|trapdoor|dungeon|flashlight_dying|low_hearts|water|car|radio|film|coin_feda|death|eye_seen> (several lines may share an event: they play one at a time, in file order, each time it happens); idle (a long quiet stretch of walking), trail (a long walk far from roads and houses), morning (the day a new door opens, with day = [N,N]). REAL VOICES: record a line, convert it (see voice/vo/RECORDING.md) and save it as voice/vo/real/<id>.m4a. If that file exists the game plays it instead of the computer voice, with no code change (and it re-times the subtitles by itself). Keep lines short: 3 to 14 words reads best. Say 'downtown', not the real name of the town.

lines.text: The square's tree, dark as a closed shop. It was supposed to be lit by now.
Bowlinghallen. Warm, loud, smells of floor polish. Safest place I know.
A church always sounds bigger inside than it looks from the street.
The river under here never freezes. It just gets quieter.
Camp Botnan. Tipis in the snow. Martin would call this roughing it.
Orresteinen. A rock the size of a house, waiting for a bus that isn't coming.
A giant globe on a hill. Nobody asked, and yet here we are.
The penstock. One very long pipe with very strong opinions about gravity.
Hamrevarden. The whole valley is down there, pretending not to look back.
Feda. All this humming. Whatever is in those wires, I am not licking it.
Home. Kettle, sofa, and a floor that growls at me sometimes.
Her door. Do not knock. Do not breathe loudly. Do not ask about the smell.
Martin's place. Empty, tidy, suspiciously quiet. He's either hiding or lost.
The market stalls. Everyone's gone home, but the gløgg is still steaming.
A cairn. Somebody stacked these stones and trusted the weather to behave.
That was a person once. Don't look at the face. Don't look at the face.
I can't move. Okay. I can blink. Blinking is something.
Lamplight. Nothing steps into it. I'm staying right here until morning.
The lantern flares and they flinch. I could get used to that.
Someone's notes. Handwriting like a spider on coffee. Worth reading, though.
Still warm. Either someone is very kind, or very close.
Snowballs. Last time I threw one at Martin, he sulked until February.
Rockets. A terrible idea, and I'm doing it anyway.
Every light is out. The whole town is holding its breath.
Dawn. Thin and grey, and the best thing I've seen all year.
There she goes. That's her way of saying good morning.
Quiet. After all that, it's actually quiet. I don't trust it. I love it.
A trapdoor. In my own building. Under my own feet. Naturally.
This was never a flat. Nobody ever paid rent for this.
Come on. Come on. The battery has opinions, apparently.
Not great. Breathe, Chris. Breathe, and then run.
Cold. Very, very cold. Note to self: never do that again.
A car. Lovely. Good chance it isn't mine, but lovely.
Static, then music, then static. Like being alive, really.
Rented a film. Nothing says everything's fine like a Friday deadline.
Coins on the road from Feda. Someone is leaving a trail, or losing a fortune.
Right. Let's agree that never happened, and try it again.
Something up on the hill is watching me. Of course it is.
Quiet night. Quiet like a held breath, not like a nap.
I know every shop in this town. Tonight, none of them knows me.
Snow squeaks underfoot. Just snow. Almost certainly just snow.
If Martin were here, he'd be talking. I miss the talking. Never telling him.
Empty streets get more crowded the longer you stare at them.
Someone's lit a window somewhere. That's enough to keep walking.
Nobody's been up here in a while.
No shops, no streetlights. Just me and a great deal of white.
Footprints ahead. Mine, I think. Probably mine.
First of December. The tree is dark, and somehow that feels personal.
Steep hill, tiny sled. My courage was not on the list.
Bowling. Chosen carefully, by someone who wants Martin to lose.
Someone's singing out there. In this cold, that takes nerve.
Funny how a coin on the road feels like a small, private gift.
Tipis tonight. I did say I'd try the outdoors again.
Something's rattling in the building. I'd blame the pipes. Quietly.
Today I find out what's behind her door. I'd rather find out tomorrow.
A globe on a hill. Of all the things to spend a morning chasing.
A very large rock. I'm told the view is worth it. I'm told a lot of things.
Jetpacks and rings. Martin is already stretching, which cannot be good.
Today ends it. One way or another, today it ends.
Decorations again. This time, the lights might actually stay up.
Another parcel from home. I'm learning to hope in small amounts.
It's wrong out there today. Everything feels one step to the left.
Christmas Eve. And the tree knows it.
The tree on the square. I'm not nervous. I'm attentive.
Bowlinghallen! Chris says it's lucky. Chris once bowled a forty and called it strategy.
A church. Very quiet. Hello? Sorry, I wasn't talking to you. Or you.
I'm fine with bridges. It's the water underneath I'm still negotiating with.
Tipis. Real ones. If anything howls, I'm sleeping in the car.
That is a very large rock. I'll climb it. Confidently. Mostly.
A giant globe, on a hill, in Norway. I've seen worse decisions today.
Follow the pipe, Martin. Worst case, it ends somewhere. Best case, soup.
Hamrevarden. Oh. Wow. Okay. Chris would say something clever here.
These wires hum like they know something I don't. Which, fair.
My house. Empty. Just me and the radiators, and the radiators are judging.
I can hear her down there, breathing. Hello, ma'am. Nothing to see.
Chris's flat. He has a kettle and no fear. I have the kettle.
Gløgg stall, empty. Somebody left in a hurry, or somebody left on purpose.
A cairn. I'll add one stone. Politely. For luck.
Okay, that's not a person. Not anymore. Walking, Martin. Calmly. Walking.
I'm frozen. Actually frozen. Is this what Chris means by stay calm?
Lamplight! Nothing's coming in. I live here now.
Flare! I did a flare! Chris is never going to believe this.
A notebook page. Someone wrote don't four times. I'm choosing to read the rest.
A thermos. Still warm. I'm drinking it. Don't tell Chris.
Snowball time. I'd like it noted that I started this out of love.
Rocket! I am absolutely in control of this. I am absolutely not.
The lights have gone. All of them. Right. Everyone stay very still.
Dawn. The sun. I could cry. I will not cry. Possibly.
That scream. Was that the witch? That was the witch. I'm fine. I'm fine.
She's gone. She's actually gone. Chris owes me a very large coffee.
A trapdoor. Under her flat. Of course there is.
A dungeon, in a block of flats. Chris, you never mentioned the dungeon.
No, no, no. Don't go dim now. I've only just started trusting you.
Hearts are low. Nerves are lower. Time for a sensible retreat.
Water! Cold! Cold! Why is it so cold?
A car. If I crash it, it was already crashed.
Somebody out there is still playing songs. That's lovely, actually.
Renting a film. Chris always picks the scary ones. Today it's my turn.
Coins on the road from Feda. Chris would pocket them silently. I'm announcing it.
Well. That wasn't ideal. Let's call it a rehearsal.
It's watching me. The big light on the hill. Hi. Hello. Please stop.
Snow on everything. It makes the whole place sound like it's keeping a secret.
I'm talking to myself again. Chris says it's a bad habit. Chris is probably right.
Just a quiet walk. A very ordinary walk. Everything is fine.
Somewhere a door just closed. I didn't hear a door. We're not discussing it.
I wonder what Chris is doing. Something brave, probably. Or reading about being brave.
The windows look warm. The shadows between them look hungry.
Nobody's walked this way in ages. I feel like I'm trespassing on winter.
No houses, no people. Just me and some rather confident trees.
Tracks in the snow. Small ones. I'm not following them. Just walking beside them.
First of December. Chris says be brave. I say stay near the tree.
A sled down a hill. What could possibly go wrong, other than everything.
Bowling today! The one thing in town where I'm unafraid. Mostly.
I can hear singing. Either carolers, or something much worse.
Coins on the road. I'm saving up for bravery. Or soup.
Tipis tonight. I packed. I packed a lot of snacks.
Chris has mail. I have a feeling about the mail.
Today we listen at her door. I'll be standing behind Chris. Supportively.
A giant globe. I'd say that's overkill, but I'm a big fan.
Climbing a rock today. A big one. I'm calling it a hill, to stay calm.
Jetpacks! The best day. Also the worst day. Hard to tell.
Today we go down there. Right. Okay. I'm ready. I'm not. I'm ready.
Decorating day. Finally, something that isn't trying to eat me.
The last parcel. I hope it's cookies. I hope there are cookies left.
Today feels thin, like a stage set. I'd rather be inside Bowlinghallen.
Christmas Eve. Chris, if you're listening: well done. Both of us.
Is that... a Marius original? Smells like a masterpiece.
Marius was here. Unfortunately.
That is not a cow. That is Marius's work.
He built a whole downtown, and this is the part he signed.
Even the carrots are keeping their distance. Smart carrots.
Rustic, I would say. Marius would say art.
So this is what a creator leaves behind. Respect. Mostly respect.
Okay, nobody tell Marius I saw it. Actually, definitely tell Marius I saw it.

lines.mood: solemn, a tiny sniff, then fond
lines.text: Well, here lies Hankie the Christmas log. Rest in peace, little buddy.
Ugh. Smells burnt. Like a bonfire that gave up halfway.
Something burned here. Recently. The smell hasn't left.
Wet ash and burnt wood. I'm not standing downwind of that.
That's not burnt cookies. That's burnt house.
Still smoking. I hope everyone got out. And the cat.
